findings.title: Async callback in `forEach` in vital reschedule discards the calendar delete promise and escapes the try/catch
findings.description: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` now returns a promise per element, but `forEach` ignores it. The `return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` value is never awaited or collected, and a rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes an unhandled rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding `try`. The reschedule can report success while calendar deletions are still pending or have failed silently. Use `for...of` or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: Async callback in `forEach` in wipemycalother reschedule discards the calendar delete promise and escapes the try/catch
findings.description: Same slip as the vital reschedule: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` drops the promise from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`, so failures bypass the `try` and deletions are not awaited. Replace with `for...of` or `Promise.all` over `map`.

findings.title: Async callback in `forEach` in trpc bookings reschedule discards the calendar delete promise
findings.description: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` has the same defect. The awaited `getCalendar` and the returned `deleteEvent` promise are not joined to the mutation's flow, so the procedure can finish before calendar cleanup completes and rejections are unhandled.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar updates run inside an un-awaited `forEach(async ...)`
findings.description: The newly added `const calendar = await getCalendar(credential);` sits inside `.forEach(async (credential) => {`. `forEach` does not wait for the callbacks, so the `updateEvent` calls queued in `apiDeletes`-style flows may still be running when the handler continues, and any error is not caught by the handler's error path.
